Property Overview
5614 W Adams Blvd • West Adams, CA 90016

The LAAA Team of Marcus & Millichap is pleased to present 5614 W Adams Boulevard, a seven-unit multifamily investment opportunity located in one of Los Angeles' fastest-growing neighborhoods. Built in 1961 and subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, the property features a desirable unit mix of all 2-bedroom, 1-bath units, averaging approximately 715 square feet each.

Ownership has made substantial capital improvements since acquiring the property in 2022, including a new roof installation (2022), backflow water preventer (2023), major central plumbing upgrades (late 2023), landscaping investment, exterior painting, and re-stuccoing (2024). Additionally, two units were fully remodeled in 2024 with permits, featuring new double-pane windows, flooring, kitchen cabinetry, appliances, in-unit washer/dryer, and mini-split HVAC systems.

Two units are currently vacant, including one that has been fully demolished and passed rough mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) inspections. This unit has been retrofitted to accommodate a washer/dryer, dishwasher, oven range, hood, refrigerator, and mini-split HVAC system. An estimated $50,000 combined is needed to complete both vacant units, offering the buyer the opportunity to finish these units to their own design specifications and immediately lease at market rents of approximately $2,500/month each.

Location: Located just west of La Cienega Boulevard, the property is walking distance to the La Cienega/Jefferson Metro Station, Cumulus District, and Whole Foods, with convenient access to Culver City, USC, Kaiser Permanente, and Downtown Los Angeles. The West Adams corridor continues to experience strong renter demand driven by its evolving retail, dining, and cultural landscape.

Acquisition Strategy
  • Suggested Offer Price — $1,750,000 (range: $1,700,000–$1,750,000). Represents approximately $145,000 below the current asking price of $1,895,000.
  • Terms Required — All-cash offer with no financing contingency. Cash certainty is essential to motivate the seller to accept a below-asking offer.
  • Timeline — Quick close targeting a 15–21 day escrow. Speed and certainty of execution are the primary levers to offset the pricing discount.
  • Renovation Budget — Approximately $50,000 combined to complete two vacant units (one gutted to studs with MEP passed; one needs cosmetic finishing). Upon completion, both units can be leased at market rents of ~$2,500/month.
  • Why This Price Works — At $250,000/unit, the offer is well below the comp average of $316,095/unit. The all-cash, quick-close terms provide the seller with certainty and speed, justifying the discount from ask. The buyer gains immediate upside through unit completion and lease-up.
Target Buyer Profile
  • Value-Add Investors — Two vacant units ready for finishing at ~$50K combined cost, with immediate lease-up to $2,500/month each. In-place rents on occupied units average $2,014, with ~20% upside through turnover.
  • 1031 Exchange Investors — All-cash, quick-close structure aligns with exchange timelines. Five occupied units provide immediate cash flow with a 6.66% current yield on day one.
  • Owner-Occupants — Opportunity to occupy one of the vacant units (or finish it to personal specifications) while collecting rent from five tenants, offsetting the majority of housing costs.
  • Small Portfolio Investors — Accessible price point under $2M in a rapidly appreciating West Adams submarket, with TOC Tier 2 density bonus potential for long-term upside.

Broad appeal across buyer segments supports competitive positioning and strong investor interest at the suggested offer level.

Pricing Rationale

The suggested offer price of $1,750,000 is supported by comparable sales data and reflects the property's current condition, including two vacant units requiring an estimated $50,000 in combined renovation costs. At $250,000 per unit, the offer sits meaningfully below the comp average of $316,095/unit, providing a built-in equity cushion from day one.

The all-cash, quick-close terms (targeting 15–21 day escrow) are designed to give the seller certainty and speed of execution—the two most compelling motivators for accepting a below-asking offer. The current asking price of $1,895,000 at a 6.15% cap rate reflects a fully stabilized value; however, with two units vacant and requiring capital to complete, the $1,750,000 offer price appropriately accounts for the renovation risk and lease-up period the buyer will absorb.

Upon completing the two vacant units (~$50,000) and leasing at $2,500/month each, the buyer achieves a pro forma NOI of approximately $143,419, representing an 8.20% yield on the $1,750,000 all-in basis (excluding renovation costs). Including the $50,000 renovation, the effective all-in basis of $1,800,000 still yields a 7.97% pro forma return—an exceptional risk-adjusted return for a West Adams multifamily asset.

Assumptions & Conditions: All returns calculated on an all-cash basis with no debt financing. Vacancy factor of 3.0% applied to gross scheduled rent. Management fee at 5.0% of effective gross income. Renovation budget of ~$50,000 is an estimate; buyer should verify costs independently. Pro forma rents of $2,500/month for renovated units are based on comparable market data and are not guaranteed. All information should be independently verified by the buyer.
